openwrt_wiki.einleitung: TP-Link Archer C20(EU) v5 is a router with a 5-port FE switch and non-detachable antennas, based on MediaTek MT7628AN + MT7610EN. It has 2 2.4GHz antennas (left and right) and one 5GHz (center). Both 2.4 antennas are soldered to the board, the 5GHz is connected using an U.FL connector.

hardware_info.USB: SoC capable, but not in the board

openwrt_wiki.create_factory_image: As all installation methods require a U-Boot to be integrated into the Image (and we do not ship one with the image) we are not able to create an image in the OpenWrt build-process. Download a [[https://www.tp-link.com/en/support/download/archer-c20/v5/#Firmware|TP-Link image]] from their Website and extract ''.bin'' file from the archive. Pay attention to regional match, i.e. if the router is EU-based, download firmware file for EU. Then download a OpenWrt sysupgrade image for the device. You may try this commands to download the TP-Link firmware: # download a firmware image archive from TP-Link site wget "https://static.tp-link.com/upload/firmware/2023/202308/20230807/Archer%20C20(EU)_V5_221028.zip" # extract .bin image from the archive and save to tpl.bin unzip -p "Archer C20(EU)_V5_*.zip" *.bin > tpl.bin # download OpenWrt sysupgrade image and save to owrt.bin wget -O owrt.bin https://downloads.openwrt.org/releases/24.10.2/targets/ramips/mt76x8/openwrt-24.10.2-ramips-mt76x8-tplink_archer-c20-v5-squashfs-sysupgrade.bin Build yourself a factory image like following: # TP-Link image: tpl.bin # OpenWrt sysupgrade image: owrt.bin # Copy a boot sector (first 131584 bytes) from the TP-Link image tpl.bin and write to the boot.bin dd if=tpl.bin of=boot.bin bs=131584 count=1 # Merge the contents of boot.bin and owrt.bin to flash.bin cat boot.bin owrt.bin > flash.bin On Windows you can use PowerShell: # Copy a boot sector (first 131584 bytes) from the TP-Link image tpl.bin and write to the boot.bin [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("boot.bin", [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("tpl.bin")[0..131583]) # Merge the contents of boot.bin and owrt.bin to flash.bin [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("flash.bin", [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("boot.bin") + [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("owrt.bin"))
openwrt_wiki.installing_web_ui: Upload the ''flash.bin'' via TP-Links firmware upgrade tool in the web-interface: Advanced Settings / System tools / Upgrade firmware
openwrt_wiki.installing_recovery:
Activate Web-Recovery by beginning the upgrade Process with a Firmware-Image from TP-Link. After starting the Firmware Upgrade, wait ~3 seconds (When update status is switching to 0%), then disconnect the power supply from the device. Upgrade flag (which activates Web-Recovery) is written before the OS-image is touched and removed after write is successful, so this procedure should be safe.

Plug the power back in. It will come up in Recovery-Mode on 192.168.0.1. When active, all LEDs but the WPS LED are off. Remember to assign yourself a static IP-address as DHCP is not active in this mode.

The ''flash.bin'' can now be uploaded and flashed using the web-recovery.
openwrt_wiki.installing_tftp: -> [[docs:guide-user:installation:generic.flashing.tftp]] Prepare an image like following (Filenames from factory image steps apply here) dd if=/dev/zero of=tp_recovery.bin bs=196608 count=1 dd if=tpl.bin of=tmp.bin bs=131584 count=1 dd if=tmp.bin of=boot.bin bs=512 skip=1 cat boot.bin >> tp_recovery.bin cat owrt.bin >> tp_recovery.bin Place ''tp_recovery.bin'' in root directory of TFTP server and listen on ''192.168.0.66/24''. Connect router LAN ports with your computer and power up the router while pressing the reset button. The router will download the image via tftp and after ~1 Minute reboot into OpenWrt.
openwrt_wiki.uboot_cli: U-Boot CLI can be activated by holding down '4' on bootup.
openwrt_wiki.dual_uboot:
This is TP-Link MediaTek device with a split-uboot feature design like a TP-Link Archer C50 v4. The first (factory-uboot) provides recovery via
TFTP and HTTP, jumping straight into the second (firmware-uboot) if no recovery needs to be performed. The firmware-uboot unpacks and executed the kernel.
openwrt_wiki.web_recovery:
TP-Link integrated a new Web-Recovery like the one on the Archer C7v4 / TL-WR1043v5 / Archer C50v4. Stock-firmware sets a flag in the "romfile" partition before beginning to write and removes it afterwards. If the router boots with this flag set, bootloader will automatically start
Web-recovery and listens on 192.168.0.1. This way, the vendor-firmware or an OpenWrt factory image can be written.

By doing the same while performing sysupgrade, we can take advantage of the Web-recovery in OpenWrt.

It is important to note that Web-Recovery is only based on this flag. It can't detect e.g. a crashing kernel or other means. Once activated it
won't boot the OS before a recovery action (either via TFTP or HTTP) is performed. This recovery-mode is indicated by an illuminated WPS-LED on
boot.

openwrt_git.nachricht:
ramips: add support for TP-Link Archer C20 v5

TP-Link Archer C20 v5 is a router with 5-port FE switch and
non-detachable antennas. It's based on MediaTek MT7628N+MT7610EN.

Specification:
- MediaTek MT7628N/N (580 Mhz)
- 64 MB of RAM
- 8 MB of FLASH
- 2T2R 2.4 GHz and 1T1R 5 GHz
- 5x 10/100 Mbps Ethernet
- 3x external, non-detachable antennas
- UART (J1) header on PCB (115200 8n1)
- 7x LED (GPIO-controlled*), 2x button, power input switch

* WAN LED in this devices is a dual-color, dual-leads type which isn't
  (fully) supported by gpio-leds driver. This type of LED requires both
  GPIOs state change at the same time to select color or turn it off.
  For now, we support/use only the green part of the LED.

Create Factory image
--------------------
As all installation methods require a U-Boot to be integrated into the
Image (and we do not ship one with the image) we are not able to create
an image in the OpenWRT build-process.

Download a TP-Link image from their Website and a OpenWRT sysupgrade
image for the device and build yourself a factory image like following:

TP-Link image:             tpl.bin
OpenWRT sysupgrade image:  owrt.bin

 > dd if=tpl.bin of=boot.bin bs=131584 count=1
 > cat owrt.bin >> boot.bin

Installing via Web-UI
---------------------
Upload the boot.bin via TP-Links firmware upgrade tool in the
web-interface.

Installing via Recovery
-----------------------
Activate Web-Recovery by beginning the upgrade Process with a
Firmware-Image from TP-Link. After starting the Firmware Upgrade,
wait ~3 seconds (When update status is switching to 0%), then
disconnect the power supply from the device. Upgrade flag (which
activates Web-Recovery) is written before the OS-image is touched and
removed after write is succesfull, so this procedure should be safe.

Plug the power back in. It will come up in Recovery-Mode on 192.168.0.1.
When active, all LEDs but the WPS LED are off.
Remeber to assign yourself a static IP-address as DHCP is not active in
this mode.

The boot.bin can now be uploaded and flashed using the web-recovery.

Installing via TFTP
-------------------
Prepare an image like following (Filenames from factory image steps
apply here)

 > dd if=/dev/zero of=tp_recovery.bin bs=196608 count=1
 > dd if=tpl.bin of=tmp.bin bs=131584 count=1
 > dd if=tmp.bin of=boot.bin bs=512 skip=1
 > cat boot.bin >> tp_recovery.bin
 > cat owrt.bin >> tp_recovery.bin

Place tp_recovery.bin in root directory of TFTP server and listen on
192.168.0.66/24.

Connect router LAN ports with your computer and power up the router
while pressing the reset button. The router will download the image via
tftp and after ~1 Minute reboot into OpenWRT.

U-Boot CLI
----------
U-Boot CLI can be activated by holding down '4' on bootup.

Dual U-Boot
-----------
This is TP-Link MediaTek device with a split-uboot feature design like
a TP-Link Archer C50 v4. The first (factory-uboot) provides recovery via
TFTP and HTTP, jumping straight into the second (firmware-uboot) if no
recovery needs to be performed. The firmware-uboot unpacks and executed
the kernel.

Web-Recovery
------------
TP-Link integrated a new Web-Recovery like the one on the Archer C7v4 /
TL-WR1043v5 / Archer C50v4. Stock-firmware sets a flag in the "romfile"
partition before beginning to write and removes it afterwards. If the
router boots with this flag set, bootloader will automatically start
Web-recovery and listens on 192.168.0.1. This way, the vendor-firmware
or an OpenWRT factory image can be written.

By doing the same while performing sysupgrade, we can take advantage of
the Web-recovery in OpenWRT.

It is important to note that Web-Recovery is only based on this flag. It
can't detect e.g. a crashing kernel or other means. Once activated it
won't boot the OS before a recovery action (either via TFTP or HTTP) is
performed. This recovery-mode is indicated by an illuminated WPS-LED on
boot.

Signed-off-by: Maxim Anisimov <maxim.anisimov.ua@gmail.com>
[adjust some node names for LEDs in DTS]
Signed-off-by: Adrian Schmutzler <freifunk@adrianschmutzler.de>

roh.openwrt_image_mk:
define Device/tplink_archer-c20-v5
  $(Device/tplink-v2)
  IMAGE_SIZE := 7616k
  DEVICE_MODEL := Archer C20
  DEVICE_VARIANT := v5
  TPLINK_FLASHLAYOUT := 8MSUmtk
  TPLINK_HWID := 0xc200005
  TPLINK_HWREVADD := 0x5
  DEVICE_PACKAGES := kmod-mt76x0e
  IMAGES := sysupgrade.bin
endef

gluon_pr_2481.titel: ramips-mt76x8: add support for TP-Link Archer C20 v5
gluon_pr_2481.text:
With this PR I would like to propose TP-Link Archer C20 v5 support. Owning a C20 v5, based on @herbetom's commit, I did the device-Integration-checklist[1], please find it here:

- [X] Must be flashable from vendor firmware
  - [X] Web interface
  - [ ] TFTP (possible[2] but not tested)
  - [ ] Other: TP-Link recovery mode (possible[2] but not tested)
- [X] Must support upgrade mechanism
  - [X] Must have working sysupgrade (`sysupgrade sysupgrade.bin` works)
    - [X] Must keep/forget configuration (`sysupgrade [-n]`, `firstboot`)
  - [X] Gluon profile name matches autoupdater image name
        -> Gluon profile name: tp-link-archer-c20-v5 (device name in ramips-mt76x8 target file)
        -> Autoupdater image name: tp-link-archer-c20-v5 (via lua get_image_name())
- [X] Reset button must return device into config mode
- [X] Primary MAC address should match address on device label (or packaging)
      -> /lib/gluon/core/sysconfig/primary_mac contains primary mac on device label
- Wired network
  - [X] should support all network ports on the device
  - [X] must have correct port assignment (WAN/LAN)
        -> Wan: eth0.2 (SW Port 0), Lan: eth0.1 (SW Ports 1-4)
- Wireless network (if applicable)
  - [X] Association with AP must be possible on all radios
  - [X] Association with 802.11s mesh must work on all radios 
  - [X] AP+mesh mode must work in parallel on all radios
- LED mapping
  - Power/system LED
    - [X] Lit while the device is on
    - [X] Should display config mode blink sequence 
          - The device has no "sys" LED, so instead the power LED is flashing
  - Radio LEDs
    - [X] Should map to their respective radio
    - [X] Should show activity
  - Switch port LEDs
    - [X] Should map to their respective port (or switch, if only one led present) 
          - only one LED present
    - [X] Should show link state and activity

One other thing to mention with this device, is that OpenWRT cannot build factory firmware[2], only sysupgrade. In order to create a first-install/ factory image one needs to download the official tp-link firmware[3] and prepend the first 131584 bytes to the sysupgrade image. This is one extra step and very easy to do. It is explained in more detail in [2].

Links:
[1] https://github.com/freifunk-gluon/gluon/wiki/Device-Integration-checklist
[2] https://git.openwrt.org/?p=openwrt/openwrt.git;a=commit;h=86e7353bff2a5de257de8ec62e782f016eed143c
[3] https://static.tp-link.com/2021/202101/20210127/Archer%20C20(US)_V5_201214.zip

antennen_je_band.wert: getrennt: zwei 2.4 GHz (links und rechts), eine 5 GHz (Mitte)
getrennt: 2.4 GHz außen links/rechts, 5 GHz Mitte

usb.bemerkung: SoC capable, but not in the board

poe_eingang.bemerkung: abgeleitet: Datenblatt nennt nur "External Power Supply: 9VDC/0.6A", kein PoE

einsatzort.bemerkung: "Restricted to indoor use" (EU-Hinweis) und "not be located in a place where it will be exposed to moisture"

montage.bemerkung: "The router can be placed on a shelf or desktop"
Foto der Unterseite zeigt zwei Schlüssellöcher links und rechts vom Typenschild; Wandmontage in Handbuch/Datenblatt nicht erwähnt

luefter.bemerkung: abgeleitet: auf den FCC-Innenfotos kein Lüfter zu sehen

led_anzahl.wert: 6 sichtbare Anzeigen: Power, 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, WPS, Ethernet, Internet (grün/orange)

reset_knopf.wert: Rückseite; gedrückt halten, bis alle LEDs aus sind = Werkseinstellung
Reset beim Einschalten gedrückt halten startet TFTP-Recovery

seriell_zugang.bemerkung: "UART (J1) header on PCB"; ob Stiftleiste bestückt ist, sagt der Commit nicht
Post 3: "similar holes for serial as in the v4"

seriell_pinbelegung.wert: J1, von vorn gesehen rechts: Front | TX - RX - GND - VCC | Rückseite; Pin 1 (dicke Linie und Dreieck im Aufdruck) = TX

seriell_baud.bemerkung: Kernel-Kommandozeile console=ttyS0,115200; Tabelle im Wiki als ungetestet auskommentiert

seriell_hinweis.wert: Unterbrechen nur im kurzen Fenster mit '4' ("switch BootType: 4: System Enter Boot Command Line Interface")

gehaeuse_oeffnen.wert: zwei Schrauben unten lösen, Oberteil abhebeln; braucht Kraft, Rastnasen brechen leicht, Gehäuse nicht zum Öffnen gedacht

bootloader.wert: U-Boot, zweistufig (factory-uboot mit TFTP-/Web-Recovery, dann firmware-uboot)

installation.wert: kein Factory-Image aus dem Build: aus TP-Link-Image die ersten 131584 Bytes vor das sysupgrade-Image setzen, dann über Web-UI, Web-Recovery oder TFTP
Web-UI (flash.bin), Web-Recovery auf 192.168.0.1 (Update abbrechen durch Stromtrennen ~3 s nach Start), TFTP: tp_recovery.bin, Server 192.168.0.66/24, Reset beim Einschalten halten
Gluon: nur sysupgrade-Image (factory = false); Erstinstallation über Web-UI mit selbst gebautem Image geprüft, TFTP nicht getestet
TFTP mit tp_recovery.bin klappt; Rückweg zur Stock-Firmware per Web-Recovery: printf \xef\xcd\xab\x89 > /dev/mtdblock8, dann Neustart

mac_label.wert: primary_mac in Gluon entspricht der MAC auf dem Typenschild

gluon_support.wert: ja, ramips-mt76x8, Image tp-link-archer-c20-v5, nur sysupgrade (factory = false)

gluon_support.bemerkung: Zugehörigkeit zu v2022.1 per GitHub-Compare geprüft (v2021.1.2 enthält ihn nicht)

bekannte_probleme.wert: WAN-LED zweifarbig, OpenWrt nutzt nur den grünen Teil
kein Factory-Image von OpenWrt; Stock-Image falscher Region kann scheitern ("Pay attention to regional match")

varianten.wert: Archer C20 V4, V5, V6, V6.20 sind verschiedene Hardware
v1 (AC750, USB), v2 (AC900, 3T3R), v4 (AC750, ohne USB) - andere Geräte

offene_faeden.grund: Fotos aus dem OpenWrt-Wiki (Platine, J1-Lötpunkte), nicht abgerufen
Außenfotos: Maß der DC-Buchse und Schlüssellöcher für Wandmontage nicht ausgewertet
Innenfotos nur grob angesehen; ob J1 bestückt ist, bei höherer Auflösung prüfen
258 Beiträge, nur 1-20 gelesen (u. a. Post 133 zur Web-Recovery)
aktuelles User Guide (EU V5) nicht geladen; FCC-Handbuch 2018 ausgewertet
Leistungsaufnahme in keiner Quelle; Testberichte (5.4 MB) evtl. mit Netzteil-Daten, DC-Buchse-Maß fehlt ebenfalls

lauf.notiz: Kernfelder belegt (Strom 9 V/0.6 A Hohlstecker mit Netzteil, innen, 5x 100 Mbit/s, 2.4 GHz 2x2 n / 5 GHz 1x1 ac, Antennen extern fest, 64/8 MB, seriell J1-Lötpunkte 115200). Offen: DC-Buchsen-Maß, Leistungsaufnahme, Wandmontage nur aus Foto abgeleitet, J1-Bestückung nicht per Foto bestätigt. Kein Werkstatt-Protokoll (nur C20i vorhanden).
